messages.author: 0886a511cd5fa3ed
messages.subject: gpcount
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to run temporary emigration models with gpcount in unmarked, however I am running into a problem when I try to add covariates to phi (availability) in the model.  When setting up the unmarkedGPC frame where are the covariates thought to affect phi supposed to be located, in the yearlySiteCovs or in obsCovs?  When I try to run the following model I get the following error message Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) : 
  contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels. Thanks in advance for your help!!


clra.umf <- unmarkedFrameGPC(y=clra.data[,3:9],
                             siteCovs=clra.data[,353:373],
                              yearlySiteCovs=list(Obs=clra.data[,73:79], Time=clra.data[,143:149],
                                          BC=clra.data[,213:219], Date=clra.data[,283:289]),
                             numPrimary=7)
(fm1 <- gpcount(~P1, ~BC, ~Obs+BC+Time+I(Time^2)+Date, clra.umf00, K=40))

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gpcount
parts:
hi Kathi,
Disclaimer: I've never used pcountOpen() so I can't say exactly what is
the problem here.
However, I believe the structure you have for "yearlySiteCovs" looks
right (one column for each year). If you have obsCovs then I think they
would be the same number of columns as "years x reps". So if you have 2
years with 3 reps then you would need 6 columns on that matrix. There was
this example from Richard's ALFL data:

library(unmarked)
alfl.umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y=alfl.data[,1:6],
siteCovs=alfl.data[,c("woody", "struct")],
# we could have yearlySiteCovs here.
obsCovs=list(time=alfl.data[,c("time1_05", "time2_05", "time3_05",
"time2_06", "time3_06", "time3_06")],
date=alfl.data[,c("date1_05", "date2_05", "date3_05",
"date2_06", "date3_06", "date3_06")]),
numPrimary=2)

Ok, so I don't think this helps you solve your problem. Is it possible
that one of your covariates is a factor with only a single level?
I suggest the following process to obtain more information:
(1) get rid of all the yearlySiteCovs and see if it runs
(2) add the covariates one at a time and see if it crashes on a specific
one.
(3) Look at the structure of that covariate and make sure things are
right.

regards,
andy

parts:
Hi Kathi -
It looks like you just have one count during each primary period.  Is that right?  Is it possible that you're having problems with gpcount because it requires data collected under the robust design with more than one count per primary period?   I think pcountOpen can handle data where there's just one count per primary period, but I don't know about gpcount.
-Erin
